@graph.description: Recipe video above. This is the best new thing I've found to make with a packet of beef mince! It's a streamlined take on koftas where spiced ground beef is cooked in raggedy chunks rather than threading on skewers. Based on the wildly popular New York Times Cooking's Smashed Beef Kebab With Cucumber Yogurt By Zaynab Issa, it's impressively fast, incredibly delicious, and there's so many ways to serve it! The original recipe is spiced with just turmeric, I wanted more kofta spicing so I used the spice mix from my Lamb Koftas. The smell when it's cooking is amazing!
recipeIngredient: 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper (, optional (for a bit spicy))
1 tsp cooking salt / kosher salt ((halve for table salt, +50% for flakes))
1/4 cup walnuts (, crumbled into large pieces with your hands - or chopped almonds or pecans)
1  large Lebanese cucumber ((Persian cucumbers), about 25cm/10" long)
3 tbsp finely sliced mint (, plus extra for sprinkling (substitute coriander/cilantro, or 2 tsp dried mint in yogurt sauce))
1 tbsp pomegranate molasses ((balsamic glaze is an excellent substitute - Note 2))

recipeInstructions.text: Cucumber Yogurt Sauce - Grate the cucumber into a bowl using a standard box grater. Add yogurt and mint, mix, then leave on the counter while you make the beef.
recipeInstructions.name: Cucumber Yogurt Sauce - Grate the cucumber into a bowl using a standard box grater. Add yogurt and mint, mix, then leave on the counter while you make the beef.

recipeInstructions.text: Smashed beef kofta - Grate the onion into a bowl using the same box grater. Add all the remaining kofta ingredients and mix well using your hands.
recipeInstructions.name: Smashed beef kofta - Grate the onion into a bowl using the same box grater. Add all the remaining kofta ingredients and mix well using your hands.

recipeInstructions.text: Raggedy lumps of meat - Heat the oil in a large non-stick pan over medium high heat. Use your hands to drop chunks of beef into the pan - about 2.5 cm/1" lumps (no need to be accurate), no rolling, just pinch off raggedy lumps. The pan will be full, it's ok, the meat shrinks.

Use your hands to drop chunks of beef into the pan - about 2.5 cm/1" lumps (no need to be accurate), no rolling, just pinch off raggedy lumps. The pan will be full, it's ok, the meat shrinks.

recipeInstructions.text: Brown first side 5 - 7 min - Leave undisturbed and cook for 5 to 7 minutes until the underside is dark golden (beef juices might come out because the pan is crowded but then it will evaporate), all the clumps of beef should be cooked through.
recipeInstructions.name: Brown first side 5 - 7 min - Leave undisturbed and cook for 5 to 7 minutes until the underside is dark golden (beef juices might come out because the pan is crowded but then it will evaporate), all the clumps of beef should be cooked through.

recipeInstructions.text: Add walnuts and cranberries - Flip the beef as best you can (there's lots of pieces so hard to be accurate, it's fine, just do your best) and leave for 1 minute to get a bit of colour on that side. Add the walnuts and cranberries then gently stir for another 1 minute. Remove from the stove.

recipeInstructions.text: Salt - Add the salt into the yogurt sauce and mix.

recipeInstructions.text: Serve - Spread the yogurt sauce on a large plate, or in 4 individual bowls. Spoon the beef over, drizzle with pomegranate molasses, olive oil, scatter with mint and serve with warm pita bread on the side.

recipeInstructions.text: How to eat - The idea here is to use the pita bread to scoop yogurt and beef straight off the plate, or you can stuff inside pita pockets! You could also make wraps and add tomato, shredded lettuce, and onion, or make rice bowls with basmati rice and chopped tomatoes on the side.

review.reviewBody: I made this last night - delicious! I served it with pitas, hummus and of course, a few chips! Having made your tasty lamb koftas several times, I may just be making them like this next time! Breaking pieces into a pan and leaving them to really brown was a brilliant idea. Thanks for another brilliant recipe xx

I had my first Kaftas as a young child. My best friend's family had to flee Lebanon before the war started back in the 70s. I will try your recipe; it will bring back wonderful memories.
